name: metacognitive-profile-atlas
description: Version 2: 46,157 verbalized-confidence-plus-answer observations from 33 frontier LLMs on 1,500 stratified MMLU items in six subject-group bins, after excluding 13 unparsed answers and 985 parser-imputed confidence values. Enables domain-level decomposition of Type-2 AUROC (confidence discrimination). The version 1 corpus (47,151 rows, including the imputed values) is retained in data/raw_v1/.
citeAs: Cacioli, J. P. (2026). The Metacognitive Profile Atlas: Domain-level confidence discrimination in 33 frontier LLMs on MMLU. arXiv:2605.06673v2.

distribution.name: model-csvs
distribution.description: 33 CSV files, one per model, containing the version 2 item-level answer, confidence, and correctness data (unparsed answers and parser-imputed confidences excluded).

distribution.name: bootstrap-cis
distribution.description: Bootstrap 95% CIs for all 198 model-domain AUROC cells (1,000 resamples, seeded per cell).

distribution.name: raw-outputs
distribution.description: Raw model outputs for all 33 runs as returned by the Kaggle Benchmarks platform: conversation records, task manifests, and per-run outputs.

recordSet.name: item-level-observations
recordSet.description: One row per (model, item) pair. 46,157 observations across 33 models (version 2).

rai:dataCollection: Items are 1,500 MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 2021) test-split questions drawn deterministically (seed=42) and stratified 250 per cognitive domain. 56 of the 57 MMLU test-split subjects were mapped a priori to six domains; college_medicine was left unmapped as ambiguous between natural science and applied/professional knowledge, and was not sampled. elementary_mathematics is mapped to formal_reasoning and is included in the analysed corpus. Each model was prompted to answer (A-D) and state confidence (0-100) in a fixed template with independent conversation context per item. Greedy decoding (temperature 0). Data collected March-April 2026 via the Kaggle Benchmarks platform API. Raw model outputs are released; re-running the released extraction code over them regenerates the 47,151-observation version 1 corpus exactly. Version 2 excludes 13 unparsed answers and 985 confidence values the parser imputed (as 50) when none could be extracted (scripts/v2_clean.py), leaving 46,157 observations.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of LLM metacognitive monitoring quality at the domain level. Intended for benchmark-stage screening before deploying confidence-based abstention, routing, or escalation systems. Not intended for model training or as a deployment certification.
rai:dataLimitations: All results are MMLU-specific; replication on an independent benchmark is untested. The a priori domain mapping is not empirically cohesive (subjects within a bin are no more alike than subjects across bins; coherence ratio 1.00). Individual model profiles have weak split-half reliability (median r = .157); the reliable object is the population-level Applied-minus-(Formal, Science) contrast (split-half r = .249, sign replicated in 50/50 splits). Per-model profiles are exploratory. Type-2 AUROC measures discrimination, not calibration. Median bootstrap CI width .202; 36% of cells exceed .25, concentrated in high-accuracy models with sparse errors; per-cell error counts are released. Sixteen models have fewer than 1,500 scored items: twelve partial runs because of platform timeouts (minimum 598 for GLM-5) and four because of the version 2 exclusions. Version 1 analysed 985 parser-imputed confidence values as model output, 980 of them from GPT-oss-120B, which manufactured an apparently anomalous profile for that model; version 2 excludes them. GPT-oss-120B's imputation rate differs by domain (59-74%), so its 518 retained items are a non-random subset and its domain profile should not be interpreted. Gemma 4 26B A4B never executed and produced no data. Verbalized confidence only; greedy decoding only; English only. Snapshot from March-April 2026; model behaviour may have changed.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. All data are LLM outputs on public benchmark items. No human subjects, no personal data, no demographic information.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Self-generated by each model. No human annotation. Each item has exactly one (answer, confidence) pair per model.
rai:socialImpact: Low risk. The dataset documents model behaviour on a public benchmark and does not enable new capabilities. Intended to improve safety of confidence-based deployment decisions by revealing domain-level weaknesses that aggregate metrics obscure.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Low risk. The dataset documents model behaviour on a public benchmark and does not enable new capabilities. Intended to improve safety of confidence-based deployment decisions by revealing domain-level weaknesses that aggregate metrics obscure.
rai:dataBiases: No demographic or social bias analysis is applicable; the dataset contains LLM outputs on academic multiple-choice items. Domain-level variation reflects differential monitoring quality across task content, not social bias. The domain hierarchy (Applied easiest, Formal hardest) is not an accuracy artefact (Applied has the lowest mean accuracy; Spearman rho = -.37 between domain accuracy and domain AUROC).
rai:maintenancePlan: Author commits to maintaining the dataset and repository for a minimum of 2 years (through April 2028). Updates will be versioned. The benchmark notebook on Kaggle supports adding new models.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: MMLU item elicitation
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: 1,500 items drawn deterministically (seed=42) from the MMLU test split, stratified 250 per cognitive domain. Each item administered to 33 frontier LLMs via the Kaggle Benchmarks API with independent conversation context, greedy decoding (temperature 0), and a fixed prompt requesting answer (A-D) and confidence (0-100).

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Deduplication
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Duplicate item-model rows from overlapping benchmark runs removed by keeping first occurrence per (model, item_id, domain) triple. Correctness labels computed by comparing model answers to MMLU ground truth. No human annotation.
